item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports modeling elapsed time and multiple interest scales, but does not establish that stronger recency weighting improves this benchmark. [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute/relative temporal and positional embeddings in self-attention, plus contrastive learning across interactions occurring in similar periods. Its key distinction: adjacent purchases separated by a week versus a month can carry different meanings. [ScaleRec (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104318) models transient interests and stable preferences through multi-scale Transformers, dual attention, and adaptive masking. These are relevant design precedents, not evidence of gains under the pinned RecHarness protocol.\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis is to retain one BERT4Rec network and add jointly learned, per-head attention biases from bucketed log time gaps between observed history events. Initialize temporal biases near zero; let training learn whether temporal proximity matters rather than impose monotonic decay. An optional jointly trained gate could balance local temporal context with global history inside that same network. This is an architectural inference from the literature, not a verified published BERT4Rec configuration. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s masked-item objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), reserved mask token, and appended-mask inference. Because the future interaction timestamp is unavailable, give mask-to-history attention a learned unknown-time relation rather than supplying the held-out target’s timestamp. Select changes using macro validation HR@10; retain one checkpoint per category."}
